purpose: Teach: 発泡/源流/ソプラノ/ジェンダーフリー/右腕/語尾/踏切/出走

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、発泡コンクリートの応用研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper on applications of foam concrete—that was your focus, right?
lines.style: Warm curiosity, gentle upward lilt on the question. Observant pause before the question, like she's checking her notes in her mind. Steady, encouraging presence.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、文化の源流を辿る人類学を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—actually, I focused on anthropology tracing the origins of culture.
lines.style: Quiet correction, not defensive. Slight hesitation on the opening, like he's gentle about the redirect. Even pace, genuine in the detail he offers.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、ソプラノ歌手の声帯研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, and your research on soprano vocal technique—
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost to herself. Slight smile in the voice like she's testing him gently. Warm but observant, letting the pause hang.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、ジェンダーフリー教育の事例を論文で扱いました
lines.en: That was my case study on gender-free education practices.
lines.style: Polite but definite. Quick correction, almost practiced. Underneath: slight embarrassment that she's wrong, but he states it plainly anyway.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 政治家の右腕的側近の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: So your work on political advisors and their influence—
lines.style: More engaged now, leaning into the pattern she's noticing. Still warm, but with a sharper attention. The voice of someone piecing something together.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、方言の語尾変化を論文で扱いました
lines.en: I actually researched dialect and the changes in sentence endings.
lines.style: Quick, polite clarification. Underlayer of quiet resignation—he knows what she's doing. Not irritated, just accepting the gentle mismatch.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、踏切事故の統計研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And the statistics on railroad crossing accidents—that was your paper?
lines.style: Slower now, more deliberate. Reflective, like she's watching the pattern complete itself. Genuine curiosity about why the topics don't match what she remembers.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、競走馬の出走時の心拍研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: No—I wrote about heart rate changes in racehorses at the start of a race.
lines.style: Final, soft correction. Tired but patient. The voice of someone used to being misunderstood, offering the truth one more time without complaint.
